Aṇathamīkathā
Jain. Apabhraṁśa. by Rayadhū. Jaina Sid. Bhās. IX. ii. p. 57. fn. 3.

Aṇṇaṅgarācārya(prativādibhayaṃkara)
of Vatsagotra; pupil of Vedāntadeśika an. Saumyajāmātṛ Muni.
--(Vedāntadeśika) Saptatiratnamālikā. Adyar II. p. 168 (a..

Aṇṇaṅgarārya
of the Śeṣa family.
--Daśakoṭiratnamālā, on the import of the word Nārāyaṇa; a reply to the Śaivite tract Navakoṭi by Kuṇigila Rāmaśāstrin.

Aṇṇamācārya(tāllapāka)
musician-composer attached to the Tirupati temple; 1408-1503 A. D.; composed Saṅkīrtanas in Telugu; great-grandfather of Tiruveṅkaṭa (Kāvyaprakāśaṭīkā,

; Amarakośavyā.-Bālaprabodhikā); see Tirupati Devasthānam Tāllapākam Telugu-Works, Vol. I. p. ii.
--Śṛṅgāralakṣaṇa (not recovered). See Tirupati Devasthānam Tāllapākam Telugu-Works, Vol. I. p. ii.
--Saṅkīrtanalakṣaṇa. On the conduct an. the singing of religious songs. Cinna Tirumala, his grandson, has written a Telugu Saṅkīrtanalakṣaṇa in the preface to which, he says that it is a. Telugu rendering of Aṇṇamācārya's Sanskrit work which was explained to him by his father. Tirupati Devasthanam Epi. Report I, p.. 281-2. 285.

Aṇṇayatātārya(caturvediśatakratuśrīśaila)

former name of the Mādhva pontiff Satyadharmatīrtha (died 1830-31). Bhr. p. 205.

Aṇṇayārya
--Daśāvatārakathāstuti. Skt. Col.. Mys. p. 4.
--Nṛsiṁhaviṁśati. Ibid. p. 4.
--Śrīnivāsastuti. Ibid. p. 4.

Aṇṇayārya
Tirumala, guru of Kandāla Śrīnivāsācārya, father of Veṅkaṭācārya (Bāṇāsuravijaya, Śg. I. p. 79).

Aṇṇayārya
I of Śrīśaila Bukkapaṭṭaṇam family; of Śaṭhamarṣaṇagotra; father of Śrīnivāsatātārya; grandfather of Veṅkaṭācārya II (Siddhāntaratnāvalī,
-6 an. other works) an. Śrīnivāsa II (Tattvamārtāṇḍa,

.
See J. of the Andhra His. Res. Soc. Vol. XIII. p.. 11-22 an. 91-92 on this, the following an. other writers of this family.

Aṇṇayārya
II of Śaṭhamarṣaṇagotra; of Śriśaila (Tirumala) Bukkapaṭṭaṇam family; son of Śrīnivāsatātārya I an. grandson of Aṇṇayārya I; younger brother of Veṅkaṭācārya II (Siddhāntaratnāvalī) an. elder brother an. guru of Śrīnivāsācārya II (Tattvamārtāṇḍa

etc.); guru of the Surapuram chief Veṅkaṭa, son of Rāghava, of the Kosala dynasty; hence referred to a. Surapuram Aṇṇayārya; pupil of Kauṇḍinya Śrīnivāsa an. his own elder brother Veṅkaṭācārya; father of Śrīnivāsa III, Veṅkaṭācārya III or Ayyā-Veṅkaṭācārya (Alaṅkārakaustubha,
(a., Gajasūtravādārtha, or Neranauviti sūtra vyākhyā, Baroda 7134,

b. 5501) an. Bucci Veṅkaṭācārya IV. Aṇṇayārya, elder brother of Śrīnivāsa who taught Veṅkaṭa (Rasikajanarasollāsabhāṇa, Śg. I. p.. 85-7) is probably this same Aṇṇaya. [Page094-b]
--Abhinavakarṇāmṛta, stotra on Kṛṣṇa in 72 verses. Bikaner 2955.
--Ācāryaviṁśatistotra. Adyar II. p. 155b. 188a.

--Tattvaguṇādarśa, a. imitation of Veṅkaṭādhvarin's Viśvaguṇādarśacampū.

Aṇṇayārya
guru of Veṅkaṭa Vīra (Rāghava ?), a. of a Pañcikā (?); criticised by Vigraham Deśika in his Asti-Brahmetiśrutyarthavicāra,

. See below Aṇṇayārya Śrīśaila of Nāvalpākkam.

Aṇṇayārya
mentioned in the introductory verse in the Utsavasaṅgraha,

Aṇṇayārya
of the Cakravarti family an. Śrīvatsagotra; son of Ahobalārya; guru of the a. of a. Prapannāmṛta,

Aṇṇayārya
guru of Deśikasudhī or Deśikadāsa (Nāthamunivijaya or Nāthamuniprapannatvasamarthana). See

Aṇṇayārya_Śrīśaila
of Nāvalpākkam; might have lived about 200 years ago; subject of the two eulogies, Aṇṇayāryamahādeśikasambhāvanā of Rāghavapāṭṭrācārya an. Aṇṇayāryamahādeśikamaṅgala of Vigraham Deśikācārya (ptd. in Grantha script a. Kumbhakonam); had realisation through Tapas a. Mahābalipuram; pupil of Vedānta Rāmānuja Saṁyamin; entered into the fourth Āśrama three or four days before death an. had the name Aparyāptāmṛta.
Probably wrote a work on viś. adv. called Setu (?). See Adyar Library Bulletin, 1940, January, MSS. Notes, p. 17.
Guru of Oratti Śrīnivāsarāghava (Rāmāyaṇasaṅgraha,

Aṇṇājiśāstrin
one of the a.s in the Nṛsiṁhasarvasva, RASB. IV. p. 82.
, same work ascribed to Aṇṇā Dīkṣita.

Aṇṇādīkṣita
son of Brahmajñāni Kṛṣṇaśāstrin of Puttūr.
--Smṛtidīpikā. Adyar.
. Is it the Smṛtidīpikā given above ?].

Aṇṇādīkṣita(śrautin)
a. alias of Veṅkaṭeśa, son of Anantanārāyaṇa Śrautin.
--Agniṣṭomasūtravṛtti subodhinī. Ujjain II. p. 8.
--Ādhānasūtrasāra. Ujjain II. p. 9. [Page095-b]
--Bodhāyanaśrautasūtravṛtti. Baroda 10948.

Aṇṇādhvarin
of Sukhāsīnapura near Kumbhakonam; real name Kṛṣṇamārya ? (see the 1st pre-col. verse,

Aṇṇādhvarin
of Gautama gotra; maternal grandfather of Perusūri (Vasumaṅgalanāṭaka.

Aṇṇābhāṇa
Mack. Mss. Restored Vol. IV. no. 117.

Aṇṇābhaṇīya
a name of the Tantradarpaṇa of Aṇṇā Śāstrin. Adyar D.

Aṇṇāmalai
See Aruṇagirinātha, commentator on the Raghuvaṁśa etc.

Aṇṇāvappayyaṅgār
a name of Vādhūla Vīrarāghavācārya of Tirumaliśai. (C. on the Uttararāmacarita etc.). Mysore I. p. 274.

Aṇṇāvaiyaṅgār
of Ātreyagotra an. Bodhāyanasūtra; son of Appanārya; of Kañjanūr near Tanjore; prepared almanacs every year a. the behest of King Śivāji, 1832-55, son of Śarabhoji, of Tanjore.
--Akṣayavarṣapañcāṅga. Adyar II. p. 66a.
--Āṅgirasavarṣapañcāṅga. Adyar II. p. 66a.
--Kālayuktipañcāṅga (acc. to Vākya).

.
--Pramodūtavarṣapañcāṅga. Adyar II. p. 67a.
--Śrīmukhavarṣapañcāṅga. Adyar II. p. 68b.

Aṇṇāśāstrin
one of the a.s in the Nṛsiṁhasarvasva. RASB. IV. p. 82.

Aṇṇāśāstrin
son of Rāma of Prayāga family; lived in Peralam village in Tanjore D..; belonged to a. Kaṇḍaramāṇikkam family.
--Tantradarpaṇa. Bhāṭṭā mīm.

Aṇṇāśāstrin
or aNNaMbhaTTa or aNNaJchAstrin real name Patañjalisūri; father of Appā Śāstrin or Periyappā Śāstrin (Śṛṅgāramañjarīsāharājīya,

) an. Vainateya II an. Viśvanātha (C. on Kṛṣṇānanda's Siddhāntasiddhāñjana; elder brother of Vainateya (C. on [Page096-b] Rucidatta's T. c. prakāśa); son of Kṛṣṇa an. grandson of Īśvara; defeated in the Court of Veṅkaṭapatirāya (Veṅkaṭa III, 1632-42), Kāmadeva an. Raṅgoji an. got from the king the village Erakara (Tanjore D.. Kumbhakonam Tq.); described a. proficient in the Dīdhiti. See
, Col. aNNAzAstrikRtacillara(prakIrNa)vAdaH ny., Savyabhicāralakṣaṇa, from which we know of a. Aṇṇāśāstrin, a. of many tracts of Navyanyāya, based on Śiromaṇi an. Gadādhara; in
-9, Appā Śāstrin is also given a. a.
